articles.title: Oxford Area High School Closed Friday After Measles Case Confirmed
articles.excerpt: The Chester County district shut the building for one day to audit staff immunity records after a measles case connected to the campus, as Pennsylvania's record outbreak tops 1,000 cases.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American families across Philadelphia's Chester County suburbs should verify MMR records now, since Pennsylvania excludes students and staff who cannot document measles immunity during an outbreak.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Putin Tells Iran's President Russia Will “Do Everything” to Help End Iran War
articles.excerpt: Vladimir Putin met Masoud Pezeshkian in Turkmenistan ahead of the CIS summit, vowing Moscow would use its influence to help settle the months-long Middle East conflict.
articles.nri_angle: The prolonged Iran war has kept oil prices volatile and Hormuz shipping constrained, feeding fuel-price and inflation pressures felt in India and by the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: “Is Ambani the Real Boss of India?” Musk Escalates Fight Over Stalled Starlink Launch
articles.excerpt: Elon Musk accused Indian “oligarchs” of blocking Starlink and then named Mukesh Ambani directly; New Delhi insists its satellite rules are fair and non-discriminatory.
articles.image_caption: A laptop displays the Starlink website. Elon Musk has accused Indian business interests of blocking Starlink's satellite-internet launch in India, directly naming Reliance chairman Mukesh Ambani.
articles.nri_angle: The Musk-Ambani fight over satellite internet could reshape connectivity and prices for millions of Indian households, including families of NRIs in rural and remote areas.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: American Oil Refiners Post Record Profits as Wars Squeeze Global Fuel Supplies
articles.excerpt: Valero, Marathon and Phillips 66 are on track for record third-quarter earnings as the Iran war, Middle East refinery damage and Ukrainian strikes on Russia drive diesel margins to historic highs.
articles.image_caption: An oil refinery — U.S. refiners like Valero and Marathon are posting record profits as wars squeeze global fuel supplies
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs, record fuel costs feed everyday U.S. inflation while surging refinery stocks have been among the market's best performers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Joins US and 13 Economies in Joint Push Against Global Industrial Overcapacity
articles.excerpt: Fifteen economies signed a USTR-released statement targeting state-backed overproduction in autos, batteries, semiconductors and solar — with China notably absent and India itself under a separate US trade probe.
articles.image_caption: A container ship — India joined the US and 13 other economies in a joint push against global industrial overcapacity.
articles.nri_angle: The excess-capacity fight shapes where global manufacturing lands — and India is pitching itself as the alternative to China, a shift with direct implications for diaspora investors and trade professionals.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pakistan Calls NYT Report of Its Jets Striking Houthis 'Fake and Fabricated'
articles.excerpt: Islamabad denied that its air force flew strike missions against the Houthis even as the Saudi-Turkey-Pakistan defence pact faces its first test in the escalating Yemen war.
articles.image_caption: The New York Times Building in Manhattan — Pakistan called the NYT's report of its jets striking Houthis 'fake and fabricated'.
articles.nri_angle: Nearly 2.5 million Indians live in Saudi Arabia and Indian shipping and travel move through the region's lanes; Pakistan's military role in the Saudi-led war complicates India's diplomacy with both Riyadh and Islamabad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Tells Nationals in Saudi Arabia to Stay Alert After Houthi Missile Strikes
articles.excerpt: The advisory followed Houthi-claimed ballistic missile attacks on Riyadh and Abha airports; Air India, IndiGo, Air India Express and Akasa cancelled Riyadh flights until October 10.
articles.image_caption: Riyadh's skyline at dusk. India advised its roughly 2.75 million nationals in the Kingdom to remain alert after Houthi-claimed missile strikes on Riyadh and Abha airports.
articles.nri_angle: About 2.75 million Indians live in Saudi Arabia — the embassy's stay-alert advisory, the no-videos rule, and flight cancellations directly affect one of the diaspora's largest communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Says Direct Benefit Transfers Saved Rs 5 Lakh Crore From Leakage
articles.excerpt: At the 10th India Mobile Congress, the Prime Minister said Rs 50 lakh crore has flowed directly to beneficiaries' bank accounts, calling the mobile phone the backbone of governance.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaks at the 10th India Mobile Congress in New Delhi. He said India's Direct Benefit Transfer system saved nearly Rs 5 lakh crore from falling into wrong hands.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs with family in India should ensure relatives' Aadhaar-bank seeding is current, since subsidies and pensions now arrive only via direct DBT transfers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russian Glide Bombs Kill at Least 30 at Kramatorsk Bus Stop
articles.excerpt: A crowded bus stop in eastern Ukraine's Donetsk region was struck around 10 a.m. Thursday; regional officials accused Russia of deliberately targeting civilians as public transport was suspended in two cities.
articles.image_caption: Firefighters extinguish the burned-out shell of a city bus in Kramatorsk after a Russian glide-bomb strike. The attack killed at least 30 people and wounded 18 on Thursday, Ukrainian authorities said.
articles.image_credit: Ukrainian State Emergency Service of Donetsk Region/Handout
articles.nri_angle: The war's ripple effects — energy and food prices, and the safety of Indian students who once studied in Ukrainian cities — keep its civilian toll relevant to diaspora readers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Deploys 26,000 Central Forces Ahead of CJP's October 10 Jantar Mantar Protest
articles.excerpt: About 11,000 additional CAPF personnel, taking total central force presence to 26,000, will guard the capital through October 12 as the Cockroach Janta Party plans a Jantar Mantar protest demanding CEC Gyanesh Kumar's resignation.
articles.image_caption: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke's October 2 post calls on supporters to march to Delhi and protest at Jantar Mantar on October 10 unless Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar resigns. Delhi has denied permission for the gathering and is deploying about 26,000 central forces across the capital through October 12.
articles.nri_angle: Diaspora readers with family in Delhi or travel plans to the capital this weekend should expect barricades across central Delhi through October 12 and avoid the Jantar Mantar area.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Brands Pakistan's Terrorism 'Frankenstein Monster' in Fiery UN Rebuke
articles.excerpt: Delivering a right of reply at the UN General Assembly's Sixth Committee, diplomat Raghoo Puri said Pakistan has lost control of the terror proxies it built — and dismissed its Masood Azhar bounty hike as eyewash.
articles.image_caption: An Indian diplomat speaks at the United Nations in New York. India's First Secretary Raghoo Puri used the General Assembly's Sixth Committee session to accuse Pakistan of doublespeak on terrorism.
articles.nri_angle: The Pahalgam attack struck tourists including holidaying families, and diaspora households follow the 26/11 justice diplomacy closely; Pakistan's terror-financing record also affects trade and remittance corridors through compliance costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Calls for Global Framework to Fight Cyber Fraud, Deepfakes
articles.excerpt: At the India Mobile Congress 2026, Prime Minister Narendra Modi urged governments, tech firms, telcos and banks to build a shared mechanism that stops digital fraud before it reaches people — and offered India's hard-won expertise.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi addresses the gathering during the inauguration of the 10th India Mobile Congress in New Delhi. He called for a global mechanism to stop cyber fraud and deepfakes before they reach people.
articles.nri_angle: The Indian diaspora sits on both sides of the fraud economy — scam call centers target NRIs abroad while elderly relatives in India are prime targets for cross-border scams — so any shared tracing mechanism would directly reduce harm to diaspora households.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Flu Arrives Early in California as Bay Area Becomes First Hot Spot
articles.excerpt: San Francisco reported its first flu death of the 2026–27 season and Santa Clara County hospitalizations ran 11 times higher than the same week last year, as health officials across California urge residents to get vaccinated now.
articles.image_caption: A healthcare worker administers a flu vaccine into a patient's upper arm. California health officials are urging residents to get vaccinated as flu season arrives early.
articles.nri_angle: With Diwali gatherings and fall travel weeks away, Bay Area and California diaspora families — especially households with school-age children and older relatives — should get flu shots now, since immunity takes up to two weeks to build.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Death Toll Reaches Three in Delhi's Seemapuri Building Collapse
articles.excerpt: A pregnant woman and two children are among the dead after the front of a four-storey building near Idgah Machhli Mandi collapsed Wednesday afternoon; eleven were rescued and an inquiry into the cause is underway.
articles.image_caption: Rescue workers and residents clear rubble after the front portion of a four-storey building collapsed in New Seemapuri, Delhi, on October 7, 2026. The death toll has risen to three — Gulafsa, 21, who was four months pregnant; a 12-year-old girl; and a toddler aged about one-and-a-half years — with eight injured taken to hospital.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs with family in Delhi's older housing colonies, the collapse underscores a structural-safety risk that enforcement drives keep missing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Diabetes Surge Threatens the Eyesight of Millions, Experts Warn
articles.excerpt: With over 101 million Indians living with diabetes and 85% never screened for eye damage, the country's new 2025 guidelines push AI-assisted retinal screening — a warning that applies to South Asian communities abroad as well.
articles.image_caption: Diabetic retinopathy causes damage to the blood vessels of the retina. Experts warn India's diabetes surge threatens the eyesight of millions.
articles.nri_angle: South Asians abroad carry elevated diabetes risk at lower BMI thresholds and younger ages, so the annual dilated eye exam pushed in India's new retinopathy guidelines matters in the US and UK too.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Cancer Trial Drug Zavondemstat Works Through Unexpected Target, Study Finds
articles.excerpt: A study in Nature Chemical Biology finds the drug acts mainly by blocking the DNA-building enzyme DHODH, not the KDM4 proteins it was designed to hit — with implications for patient selection in trials.
articles.image_caption: A 3D illustration depicts cancer cells with branching tendrils against a tissue-like background. A study in Nature Chemical Biology reports that the clinical-trial drug zavondemstat kills cancer cells mainly by blocking the enzyme DHODH, not the KDM4 proteins it was designed to target.
articles.nri_angle: The story is a cautionary data point for precision oncology: trial enrollment is only as useful as the accuracy of the mechanism the drug is assumed to hit, a standard that applies to patients wherever trials run.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tropical Storm Isaias Takes Aim at Gulf Coast as Season's First Hurricane
articles.excerpt: Tropical Storm Isaias formed Wednesday in the Gulf of Mexico with 50 mph winds and is forecast to strengthen into a Category 2 hurricane before landfall Friday night or Saturday along the Mississippi, Alabama or Florida panhandle coast.
articles.image_caption: NOAA satellite image of Tropical Storm Isaias in the Gulf of Mexico on Oct. 7, 2026. The storm is forecast to strengthen into a Category 2 hurricane before making landfall late Friday or early Saturday on the northern Gulf Coast.
articles.nri_angle: Significant Indian-American communities in the Gulf Coast cities under watch — Mobile, Gulfport, Pensacola, Tallahassee — face the storm's projected landfall; federal advisories urge all residents to finalize preparations.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Modi Pitches Secure, Open Maritime Order as Sagarmanthan Summit Opens in Delhi
articles.excerpt: The third edition of Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue runs October 7–9 with 1,200 delegates from nearly 75 countries, as India positions itself as a convenor on ocean governance amid mounting pressure on global sea lanes.
articles.image_caption: An announcement graphic for the third edition of Sagarmanthan: The Great Oceans Dialogue, held in New Delhi from October 7 to 9, 2026. Prime Minister Narendra Modi sent a message to the summit calling for a free, open and secure maritime order.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora in Gulf and Southeast Asian port economies, India's push to set the rules of maritime trade directly affects shipping jobs, energy flows and the remittance corridors that run through them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Delhi Building Collapse Kills Child, Traps Several as Rescue Continues in Seemapuri
articles.excerpt: The front portion of a four-storey building in New Seemapuri came down around 3:30 pm on Wednesday, killing a five-year-old and injuring at least seven; residents say cracks appeared after Tuesday night's Uttarakhand earthquake tremors.
articles.image_caption: Rescue workers and residents clear rubble after the front portion of a four-storey building collapsed in New Seemapuri, Delhi, on October 7, 2026. A child was killed and at least seven people were injured; the cause of the collapse is under investigation.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora, the collapse is another grim reminder of India's urban building-safety crisis — a concern for families with property and relatives in Delhi's dense neighborhoods.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russia Welcomes India's Ceasefire Push as Kyiv Weighs Truce Proposal
articles.excerpt: Kyiv called India’s proposal the broadest of four ceasefire offers, covering energy infrastructure and the Black Sea — as Moscow publicly embraced New Delhi’s diplomatic role.
articles.image_caption: A composite photo showing Prime Minister Narendra Modi with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy (left) and with Russian President Vladimir Putin (right). Kyiv and Moscow both publicly welcomed India’s ceasefire proposal this week.
articles.nri_angle: India’s rising diplomatic weight — publicly acknowledged by both Moscow and Kyiv — is a marker of status for the diaspora, while any ceasefire progress would ease the energy-price shocks of the past four years.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Opposition 'Vote Theft' Protests Cloud Modi's 25-Year Milestone
articles.excerpt: Narendra Modi marked a quarter-century in public office with a new “We will do it” rallying cry, even as Delhi police fortified the Election Commission of India against another day of opposition protests over voter-list revisions.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi speaks at a podium during a public event. Modi marked 25 years in public office on October 7, 2026, with the Viksit Bharat Sankalp Sabha in New Delhi.
articles.nri_angle: The milestone showcases Modi’s political endurance for the diaspora’s most-watched leader, while the opposition’s electoral-integrity campaign shapes how Indians abroad discuss Indian democracy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CJI to Decide Fate of Plea to Recall Split Verdict on Election Commission Law
articles.excerpt: A curative plea argues Justice Satish Chandra Sharma’s undisclosed family link to the Election Commission vitiates the September 23 split verdict on the CEC appointment law — and only the Chief Justice can decide what happens next.
articles.image_caption: Justice Surya Kant, the Chief Justice of India, will decide how the Supreme Court handles the curative plea against part of its September 23 split verdict on the Election Commissioners appointment law.
articles.nri_angle: The Supreme Court’s handling of the election-chief appointment law tests the credibility of the institution that runs the world’s largest election — a matter of direct interest to NRIs watching Indian democracy from abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Oman Evacuates Injured Crew From Tanker Struck in Hormuz Attack
articles.excerpt: Twelve of the MT On Peace's 19 crew were injured, including 11 Indians, in the latest of at least seven tanker attacks near the strait in early October; India condemned the strike and thanked Oman.
articles.image_caption: Cargo ships and a small boat move through open water in the Gulf region. Twelve of the 19 crew of the Panama-flagged MT On Peace were injured when the tanker was struck by a projectile while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.
articles.nri_angle: Eleven of the 12 injured crew are Indian nationals, underscoring how often Indian seafarers — who form a large share of global shipping crews — are caught in the crossfire of attacks on Gulf shipping lanes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: FIR Filed After Rahul, Priyanka Gandhi Sit-In at Akashvani Bhawan
articles.excerpt: Delhi Police booked the Gandhi siblings and INDIA bloc MPs for forcibly entering the premises during Tuesday's march against the Election Commission, after an eight-hour dharna that saw around 260 protesters detained.
articles.image_caption: Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi Vadra sit with fellow MPs under a tree inside the Akashvani Bhawan premises in New Delhi. The leaders staged an eight-hour dharna after police stopped the INDIA bloc march toward the Election Commission headquarters on Tuesday.
articles.nri_angle: Election-integrity battles are among the most closely followed Indian political stories in the diaspora, where the imagery of Rahul Gandhi waving the tricolour atop a police barricade is likely to dominate NRI political conversation for days.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pennsylvania Measles Outbreak Tops 1,000 Cases, Largest in US in Three Decades
articles.excerpt: State health officials confirmed 1,004 cases as of Oct. 5, with 198 hospitalizations and five deaths — all in unvaccinated people — as the US endures its worst measles year since 1991.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora families traveling between the US and India, the outbreak is a practical warning to check MMR vaccination records before flying, since measles spreads easily in airports and on planes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: All 23 Indian Crew Rescued After Drone Attack Sets Tanker Ablaze Off Sochi
articles.excerpt: The Liberian-flagged crude carrier Aframax Rio was struck by unmanned drone boats off Russia's Black Sea coast on October 6; emergency crews rescued all 23 Indian crew members with no injuries reported.
articles.nri_angle: All 23 crew were Indian nationals — a direct safety concern for the families in India whose relatives work the Black Sea and Gulf shipping routes, and a reminder of India's outsized presence in the global merchant navy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaishankar Meets Ghana's Mahama as Accra Courts Indian Pharma Investment
articles.excerpt: Opening a five-day tour of Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire and Ethiopia, the foreign minister's Accra visit centred on pharmaceuticals, agriculture and industrialisation — with Mahama pitching a rebounding economy to Indian investors.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar speaks at a diplomatic meeting. He met Ghana's President John Mahama in Accra on Tuesday at the start of a five-day tour of Ghana, Côte d'Ivoire and Ethiopia.
articles.nri_angle: Ghana hosts a long-standing Indian business community; Indian pharma firms are already the biggest suppliers of affordable medicines to West Africa, and Mahama's pitch could open new manufacturing partnerships for diaspora entrepreneurs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Union Cabinet Gives Modi Standing Ovation, Passes Resolution Marking 25 Years in Office
articles.excerpt: The cabinet resolution traces ten threads from Modi's Gujarat years to national policy — and came alongside approval of a Rs 10,000 crore SME Growth Fund and a new national transport authority.
articles.image_caption: Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The Union Cabinet passed a resolution congratulating him on 25 years of continuous leadership as head of government.
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora, the milestone frames a leader many NRIs have watched transform from a regional figure into a global statesman; the 25-year narrative will shape how India's story is told to the world in the years ahead.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nobel Physics Prize Goes to Francis Halzen for Capturing 'Ghost Particles' From Deep Space
articles.excerpt: The Belgian physicist's decades-long project — thousands of light sensors buried in Antarctic ice — opened a new kind of astronomy based on neutrinos, the elusive 'ghost particles' of the cosmos.
articles.image_caption: Physicist Francis Halzen poses for a portrait. He won the 2026 Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on the IceCube Neutrino Observatory and the discovery of high-energy neutrinos from deep space.
articles.nri_angle: Pure global science news with no direct diaspora impact; noted briefly as a milestone in international big science that Indian science students and researchers follow closely.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Attack on Panama-Flagged Tanker in Hormuz Injures 12 Crew, Including 11 Indians
articles.excerpt: India condemned the projectile strike on MT On Peace, whose 19-member crew included 17 Indian nationals, as the latest in a wave of attacks on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.image_caption: A commercial tanker transits open water with a small boat nearby. The Panama-flagged MT On Peace was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on October 6, injuring 12 crew members, 11 of them Indian nationals.
articles.nri_angle: Indians form one of the largest groups in the global seafaring workforce, and Indian crew have been injured or killed in multiple Hormuz strikes this year, making the attacks a direct concern for thousands of Indian families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IIT Bombay Rolls Out Wellness, Hostel and Exam Reforms After Student Suicide Row
articles.excerpt: After weeks of protests following a student's death, the institute promises twin-sharing hostels for all years, wall-mounted fans, postponed mid-semester exams, and a student-led rewrite of invigilation rules.
articles.image_caption: IIT Bombay campus in Powai, Mumbai. The institute has rolled out wellness, hostel and exam reforms after the death of second-year student Sahil Wakode on September 18.
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of diaspora families send children to IITs each year; the safety and exam reforms directly affect NRI parents weighing Indian higher education and IIT Bombay's standing as India's flagship technology institute.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Serum Institute's Cervavac Gets WHO Prequalification, Opening Path to UN Vaccine Supply
articles.excerpt: The Pune-made, gender-neutral HPV vaccine's WHO prequalification is Serum Institute's 32nd and makes CERVAVAC eligible for procurement by UN agencies for immunization programs worldwide.
articles.image_caption: Vaccine vials. Serum Institute's Cervavac has received WHO prequalification, opening the path to wider global supply.
articles.nri_angle: With an India-made, WHO-prequalified HPV vaccine eligible for UN procurement, Indian families everywhere gain an affordable path to protecting both daughters and sons against HPV-related cancers — and India's own immunization program may follow with a domestic rollout.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nepal Ends Flood Search With 5,285 Still Missing, Including 189 Indians
articles.excerpt: Forty days after the August 26 Bhotekoshi-Trishuli floods, Kathmandu called off search and rescue with 1,455 confirmed dead, recommended a $3.62 billion reconstruction budget and shifted to rehabilitation.
articles.image_caption: Satellite imagery of the Nepal–China border region on 24 August 2026, two days before the deadly August 26 floods in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers.
articles.nri_angle: 189 Indians are among the 5,285 missing in the Nepal floods, and as Kathmandu begins the legal process of declaring the missing dead, affected Indian families should watch for consular guidance on documentation and compensation claims.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: New York Declares Measles Disaster Emergency as Rural Outbreak Spreads to 18 Counties
articles.excerpt: Governor Kathy Hochul declared a statewide disaster emergency on October 5 after 108 measles cases this year, expanding who can test and vaccinate as the US endures its worst measles year since 1991.
articles.image_caption: A measles alert sign posted at Cohen Children's Medical Center in New York lists symptoms — fever, rash, cough and red eyes — and instructs symptomatic patients to wear a mask and report to the front desk. New York’s governor declared a statewide disaster emergency on October 5 as measles cases spread across 18 rural counties.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American families in New York and New Jersey, many in the suburban and upstate counties hit by the outbreak, should check their children's two-dose MMR vaccination records as the state pushes an emergency vaccination drive through November 4.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India, UAE Launch Third Mountain Guardian Exercise in Uttarakhand Hills
articles.excerpt: The fortnight-long exercise, running October 5–18 at the Foreign Training Node in Chaubatia, brings 92 troops from both armies together for mountain warfare drills including drone operations and surveillance-grid training.
articles.image_caption: Indian and UAE servicewomen pose during Exercise Mountain Guardian in Uttarakhand. Ninety-two personnel from both armies are training together at Chaubatia from October 5 to 18, with a focus on mountain warfare.
articles.nri_angle: The UAE hosts one of the world's largest overseas Indian communities, and a deeper military partnership adds a hard-security pillar to a relationship that already binds the two countries on trade, energy, and people-to-people ties.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Pune Lab's HPV Self-Sampling Kit Aims to Expand Cervical Cancer Screening
articles.excerpt: Greenarray Labs has launched CerviSens, a vaginal self-sampling kit for high-risk HPV testing that skips the speculum exam. A 203-sample validation study reported 98.0% sensitivity and 99.4% specificity versus clinician collection.
articles.image_caption: Greenarray Labs representatives at the launch of CerviSens, the company’s HPV self-sampling kit, in Pune. The kit allows women to collect their own vaginal sample for high-risk HPV testing without a speculum examination.
articles.nri_angle: Many NRI families arrange health checkups for relatives in India; a validated self-sampling option is worth flagging to women back home who have skipped cervical screening, and India's screening gap is a known concern in diaspora health philanthropy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: US Marine Arrested After Strangling Death of Japanese Woman in Okinawa
articles.excerpt: Lance Corporal Devin Jacob Ballard, 20, was arrested on suspicion of murder and robbery after Anna Yagi, 39, was found dead in a Naha hotel room. Japan's prime minister lodged a formal protest and demanded full US cooperation.
articles.image_caption: Image: @ABC via X
articles.nri_angle: The case will be watched in New Delhi, where India's deepening defence ties with the United States and Japan run through the Quad — and where past Okinawa incidents have fed public debate about the costs host communities pay for foreign military presence.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Two Killed, Indian Seafarer Injured as Russian Drone Sinks Turkish Cargo Ship
articles.excerpt: A Russian drone strike set fire to the Turkish-owned cargo vessel Royad Mammadov in the Black Sea, killing the captain and one other crew member. Three Indian nationals were aboard; one was injured and is receiving treatment in Romania.
articles.image_caption: Image: @visegrad24 via X
articles.nri_angle: India supplies a large share of the world's merchant seafarers, and Indian crew routinely serve aboard foreign-flagged cargo ships transiting the Black Sea — putting Indian nationals directly in the line of fire as drone attacks on civilian shipping escalate.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BJP drops Hardeep Puri, Smriti Irani in fresh UP Rajya Sabha slate of 8
articles.excerpt: The BJP announced an entirely new slate for the October 16 biennial elections to ten Rajya Sabha seats from Uttar Pradesh, with no sitting member renominated and two Union ministers left out.
articles.image_caption: Hardeep Singh Puri, former Union minister. (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Uttar Pradesh's Rajya Sabha bloc shapes legislation touching the diaspora — emigration, citizenship and fiscal bills — and Puri's exclusion raises the question of who holds the petroleum portfolio, with direct relevance to energy prices.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Thailand floods kill 31 as forecast warns of more rain and flash flooding this week
articles.excerpt: The Interior Ministry confirmed 31 deaths from flooding since September 16, as meteorologists forecast thunderstorms and heavy rain across upper Thailand through Wednesday.
articles.image_caption: Floodwaters in Hat Yai, Songkhla province, during Thailand's 2010 floods — file photo. (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Thailand is a top destination for Indian travellers and home to a large Indian expatriate community; with Diwali season nearing, travellers should allow extra transit time and keep plans flexible as floods disrupt roads while airports and city rail keep running.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Sitharaman: India-US trade talks hit plateau as tariff pressure narrows room for deal
articles.excerpt: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman told the Munich Leaders Meeting that India-US trade negotiations have reached a point where further give and take is "very, very difficult," as a new US law threatens up to 100% tariffs over Russian oil purchases.
articles.image_caption: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman at an official event. She said on October 5 that India-US trade talks have hit a plateau, with further concessions very difficult for both sides.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora in the US, a stalled interim deal keeps tariff overhang on textiles, gems and engineering goods exported from India, with no quick relief for exporters or the rupee's exchange math.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Three Doctors Turn Delhi–Aizawl Flight Into a Flying Emergency Ward
articles.excerpt: A passenger with chronic kidney disease suffered severe oxygen desaturation mid-flight — and three doctors travelling on board improvised a ward in the cabin until the plane landed in Aizawl.
articles.image_caption: An Air India aircraft; the Delhi–Aizawl flight where three doctors attended to a passenger's mid-air medical emergency
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora flying long-haul to India with elderly parents or chronic conditions, this rescue is a reminder to keep medical records and prescriptions in cabin baggage and brief the cabin crew on boarding.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaishankar Calls US a 'Lonelier Power', Urges Middle Path Between America and China
articles.excerpt: At the Munich Leaders Meeting, the external affairs minister said Washington had deliberately drifted, China is rising sharply, and middle powers must navigate between them with a 'Goldilocks' balance.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, who described the US as a 'lonelier power' at the Munich Leaders Meeting
articles.nri_angle: For the diaspora, this is the clearest articulation of the foreign-policy weather they live in: Jaishankar's balancing act between a repositioning America and an assertive China will shape the trade, technology and immigration policies that touch Indians abroad.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: IRDAI's Insurance Commission Overhaul Sparks Fears for One Million Brokers' Jobs
articles.excerpt: The regulator wants to cap commissions and cut insurers' expense limits by a third; brokers say the maths will kill jobs and leave small-town customers unserved.
articles.image_caption: A blue keyboard key labelled "insurance" with an umbrella icon on a white keyboard. IRDAI has proposed caps on insurance commissions and a one-third cut in insurers' expense limits, sparking a fight with the brokers' industry body over jobs.
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs holding Indian life and health policies, the fight is worth watching: leaner distribution economics could mean cheaper premiums and cleaner sales practices, or thinner broker networks in smaller towns where insurance penetration is lowest.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ukraine's Robot Offensive Reclaims Donetsk Villages as Winter Approaches
articles.excerpt: Explosives-packed BTR-60s driven by remote control helped Ukraine retake villages in Donetsk, while an ex-minister's new "Army of Robots" project promises to mechanise the war's deadliest jobs.
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, the operation is a gauge of the war's trajectory: India's balanced posture on the conflict, the war's drag on energy and food prices, and the safety of remaining Indian nationals in Ukraine all turn on how long the fighting lasts.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Flydubai Hijack Suspect Likely Acted Alone, Investigators Say, as Australia Link Emerges
articles.excerpt: Israeli officials say early evidence points to a lone attacker with no established group or state backing, while Australian agencies examine the Omani co-pilot's 2015-2017 residence on a student visa.
articles.image_caption: A flydubai Boeing 737 in flight. Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv was targeted in an attempted hijacking on September 30, with 174 passengers aboard.
articles.nri_angle: The flight's captain, Smit Machchhar, is of Indian origin and was hailed as a hero for saving 174 passengers — a point of pride and attention for Indian travelers on Gulf routes.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Right to Vote in 'Great Peril,' Justice Nariman Warns as Executive Grip Tightens
articles.excerpt: In a September 27 oration, the former Supreme Court judge cited 90 lakh exclusions in West Bengal's voter-roll revision and called the executive's grip on Election Commissioner appointments a "red flag."
articles.image_caption: Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman, former Supreme Court judge of India, who warned that the right to vote is in 'great peril'
articles.nri_angle: India's standing as the world's largest democracy rests on credible elections; NRIs who defend that record abroad have the most to lose when a former Supreme Court judge says the right to vote is in peril.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NASA Astronaut Jessica Meir Shares Dazzling Moonlit Earth View From Space
articles.excerpt: The Crew-12 commander posted the "Milky Way with a Moonlit Earth" clip on X days before her return from the International Space Station, calling it motivation for NASA's Artemis program.
articles.image_caption: A view of Earth from orbit with the International Space Station solar arrays visible against a star-filled sky. NASA astronaut Jessica Meir posted a video of a moonlit Earth from space during her Crew-12 mission this week.
articles.nri_angle: Moments like Meir's moonlit video travel fast across the Indian diaspora, where Indian-origin astronauts such as Sunita Williams have turned NASA missions into shared community events.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Amritsar Police Bust Pakistan-Linked Terror Module, Seize AK-47 and Grenades
articles.excerpt: Amritsar Rural Police arrested 28-year-old truck driver Navjot Singh and recovered an AK-47 rifle, two hand grenades and nine live cartridges allegedly pushed across the border by drone.
articles.image_caption: Punjab Police officers address the media in Amritsar after announcing the bust of a cross-border terror module on Sunday. Police recovered an AK-47 rifle, two hand grenades and ammunition allegedly pushed into India by drones.
articles.nri_angle: The large Punjabi diaspora in Canada, the US and the UK closely tracks border-security developments, and many families still live in the Tarn Taran-Amritsar belt where the module was operating.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russian Drone Strikes Kyiv Bridge as Germany's Merz Arrives to Sirens
articles.excerpt: Merz landed in Kyiv to pledge €1 billion in military aid and a joint drone-production deal as Russia's defence ministry said it would intensify strikes on Ukrainian military-industrial targets.
articles.image_caption: German Chancellor Friedrich Merz is greeted at a Kyiv railway station on Sunday during his visit to Ukraine. His arrival coincided with a Russian drone strike on the city’s Pivnichnyi Bridge, which injured two people.
articles.nri_angle: Germany hosts Europe's largest Ukrainian refugee population and a large Indian diaspora, both watching how the new aid package and energy-repair commitments affect Berlin's defence spending and winter energy costs.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Jaishankar Says India Has Gone 'Beyond Advocacy' in Russia-Ukraine Conflict
articles.excerpt: At the Munich Leaders Meeting, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said New Delhi is now holding direct talks with both Moscow and Kyiv on Black Sea shipping, grain and energy exports, and 'non-attack possibilities'.
articles.image_caption: External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar, who said India has gone 'beyond advocacy' in the Russia-Ukraine conflict at the Munich Leaders Meeting.
articles.nri_angle: India's deeper diplomatic engagement signals New Delhi's confidence in its standing with both Moscow and Kyiv — and its ability to protect the energy and trade interests that affect Indian households and diaspora businesses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Russian Drones Destroy Indian-Run Kusum Pharma Plant in Ukraine, One Killed
articles.excerpt: The main structure of the Kusum Group's Sumy facility was largely destroyed in Sunday's strike, which killed one worker and injured several others. The company puts its losses at at least ₹400 crore.
articles.image_caption: A plume of dark smoke rises from an industrial building after a drone strike. The aftermath of the Russian drone attack that largely destroyed the Kusum Group’s pharmaceutical plant in Sumy, Ukraine, killed one worker and injured several others.
articles.nri_angle: An Indian-run pharmaceutical company that grew from exporting Indian medicines to Ukraine into a major local manufacturer has lost its flagship Ukrainian plant to the war, putting hundreds of Ukrainian jobs and an Indian business success story at risk.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: LGBTQ Influencer Mad Sandhu Shot Dead in Amritsar, Sparking Punjab Law-and-Order Row
articles.excerpt: Mad Sandhu, a makeup artist with 2.26 lakh Instagram followers, was gunned down by two motorcycle-borne men on Saturday evening; the BJP and Congress blamed the AAP government's law-and-order record as police said they had leads.
articles.image_caption: Makeup artist and LGBTQ influencer Mad Sandhu in a photo from his Instagram account. Sandhu, who had about 2.26 lakh followers, was shot dead in Amritsar on October 3, 2026.
articles.nri_angle: Punjab's large overseas diaspora follows law-and-order developments closely given family ties and safety concerns back home; the killing also touches diaspora conversations on LGBTQ visibility and safety in Punjabi society.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Indian-Origin Men Face Extortion, Weapons and Drug Charges in BC Task-Force Sweep
articles.excerpt: Langley RCMP's 16-month Project E_PURSUANCE ended with arrests, firearms and drug seizures — and more charges are expected across BC and Alberta.
articles.nri_angle: The extortion wave gripping BC's South Asian business community has become one of the top diaspora safety issues in Canada; these arrests are the biggest scalp yet for the province's anti-extortion task force, and victims coming forward made it possible.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: California Will Fine Robotaxi Operators Up to $10,000 Per Vehicle for Blocking First Responders
articles.excerpt: Senate Bill 1246 requires local incident technicians, U.S.-based remote drivers and fleet-status alerts — with penalties starting July 2028.
articles.image_caption: A Waymo robotaxi on a San Francisco street. California's SB 1246, signed by Governor Gavin Newsom, fines operators up to $10,000 per vehicle that blocks first responders for more than 30 minutes.
articles.nri_angle: Robotaxi operators like Waymo employ thousands of engineers and operations staff across California, including many Indian engineers in the autonomous-vehicle sector — the new U.S.-based remote-driver rule reshapes how those fleets are staffed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: London, Ontario Husband Charged With Second-Degree Murder in Death of Indian-Origin Mother of Two
articles.excerpt: Raman Devi died September 15 after suffering critical injuries at her Chelton Road home; her husband Mandeep Singh, 41, has been charged and police are investigating the death as a femicide.
articles.nri_angle: The death of Raman Devi — whose mother had travelled from India to help raise her grandchildren — underscores the vulnerability of immigrant families in Canada and the community support systems, from gurdwaras to helplines, that surround them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Rebuts Pakistan at UN: J&K and Ladakh Are Integral, Says Envoy
articles.excerpt: First Secretary Petal Gahlot used India's Right of Reply at the 81st UN General Assembly to reject Shehbaz Sharif's remarks on Kashmir and the Indus Waters Treaty, accusing Pakistan of cross-border terrorism.
articles.image_caption: The UN General Assembly hall in New York, where India exercised its Right of Reply at the 81st session
articles.nri_angle: For the Indian diaspora, the UNGA exchange coincides with the 25th anniversary of September 11 — a reference Gahlot herself invoked — and follows the Pahalgam attack that killed 26 civilians in Kashmir.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Unlikely to Face Food or Fertiliser Crisis Despite Global Headwinds, Says Panagariya
articles.excerpt: The 16th Finance Commission chairman told ANI that strengthened fertiliser supplies and India's proven ability to absorb energy shocks mean the country need not fear the global food crisis Jaishankar warned of.
articles.image_caption: Arvind Panagariya, chairman of the 16th Finance Commission, speaks at a press event. He told ANI that India is unlikely to face a major food or fertiliser crisis despite continuing global conflicts.
articles.nri_angle: New Delhi is simultaneously warning of global food-crisis risk abroad and insisting India's own supplies are secure — the reassuring signal for diaspora investors and families.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: CHIME Telescope Catches 8-Billion-Year-Old Hydrogen Glow, Opening New Window on Dark Energy
articles.excerpt: Using only its own observations, the Canadian radio telescope detected neutral hydrogen from the young universe — with Raman Research Institute scientists in the collaboration — validating a new technique to map cosmic expansion.
articles.image_caption: The CHIME radio telescope at night near Penticton, British Columbia, with the Milky Way overhead. CHIME detected neutral hydrogen from about 8 billion light-years away, validating a new technique to study cosmic expansion.
articles.nri_angle: Bengaluru's Raman Research Institute is part of the international collaboration behind a landmark cosmology result, underlining Indian science's place at the frontier.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Five Indian Seafarers Rescued After Projectile Strikes Kuwait-Flagged Tanker in Strait of Hormuz
articles.excerpt: The Indian Embassy in Oman coordinated the rescue of the five crew members aboard MT Kazimah III and brought them safely ashore, amid heightened monitoring of thousands of Indian seafarers in the region.
articles.image_caption: Smoke rises from a tanker at sea after an apparent projectile strike. The Kuwait-flagged MT Kazimah III was hit in the Strait of Hormuz; five Indian crew members were rescued and brought ashore safely.
articles.nri_angle: Thousands of Indian seafarers work the Gulf shipping lanes — this rescue highlights both their physical risk and the consular network backing them.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Boiler Explosion at Andhra Pradesh Pharma Unit Kills Four, Injures Ten
articles.excerpt: A boiler exploded at Till Healthcare's tablet-manufacturing plant in Sri City, Tirupati district, during the night shift, killing four workers and injuring at least ten. Rescue operations continued through the day as the state ordered a safety audit of the industrial zone.
articles.image_caption: An inset view shows debris at the Sri City pharmaceutical unit where the boiler exploded, alongside Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister Pawan Kalyan. Four workers were killed and at least ten injured; Pawan Kalyan ordered a comprehensive safety audit of the industrial zone.
articles.nri_angle: The blast struck an Andhra Pradesh industrial corridor closely tied to diaspora families, highlighting why Indians abroad need verified casualty reporting and underscoring the role of India's private hospital network when district facilities are overwhelmed.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: OpenAI Fires Three Researchers for Mishandling Sensitive Information
articles.excerpt: The ChatGPT-maker said three safety researchers violated policies by mishandling sensitive information outside established procedures — but what exactly was shared, and with whom, remains unclear.
articles.image_caption: The OpenAI logo; the AI company fired three researchers for mishandling sensitive information.
articles.nri_angle: The fight over AI safety norms is unfolding across the US AI labs where Indian-origin engineers and researchers form a major share of the technical workforce, making OpenAI's line-drawing on information handling and internal dissent directly relevant to the diaspora's largest tech cohort.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Putin's Nuclear Warning Over Kaliningrad Exposes the Suwalki Gap's Peril
articles.excerpt: Putin said a direct attack on Kaliningrad would put Moscow's full arsenal on the agenda "inevitably and immediately" — a warning that spotlights the Suwalki Gap, NATO's exposed 65-km land link to the Baltic states, and the Baltic shipping lanes India depends on for Russian oil.
articles.image_caption: A briefing screen shows a map of Kaliningrad, Russia's Baltic exclave, wedged between Poland and Lithuania, flanked by NATO, EU, Polish, and Lithuanian flags. On October 1, 2026, President Vladimir Putin warned that a direct attack on the exclave would put Moscow's full arsenal on the agenda "inevitably and immediately."
articles.nri_angle: Indian students study in Kaliningrad, and Indian refiners depend on Baltic Sea lanes for seaborne Russian crude, so escalation in the exclave would hit Indian families and fuel prices directly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Guwahati Nightclub Horror: Video Shows Woman Stripped, Assaulted By Bouncers
articles.excerpt: A viral video shows a woman being stripped and beaten by bouncers at 'The Locals' disco club in Guwahati's Khanapara area; accounts of what triggered the violence conflict, and Guwahati Police have registered a case and opened an investigation.
articles.image_caption: A blurred still from the viral video shows several men standing around a person on the floor of a basement in a Guwahati building. The video, which surfaced after a Thursday night incident at 'The Locals' disco club in Khanapara, allegedly shows bouncers stripping and beating a woman; Guwahati Police have registered a case and opened an investigation.
articles.nri_angle: For diaspora women visiting Guwahati or with family there, the case is a stark reminder that nightlife safety in parts of India remains precarious — private club security staff can themselves become the source of danger.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Putin Pushes New Russia-India Trade Corridor as Hormuz Crisis Bites
articles.excerpt: Vladimir Putin says Russia is ready to finance the International North-South Transport Corridor with India and that Azerbaijan has agreed to its leg — but the project hinges on Iran completing its section.
articles.image_caption: Russian President Vladimir Putin gestures while speaking at a forum against a blue backdrop. He pitched deeper trade and transport links with India, including the International North-South Transport Corridor, amid disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.
articles.nri_angle: A working INSTC would cut freight costs for Indian exporters and give India an energy and trade route less exposed to Hormuz shipping disruptions, with a direct line to fuel prices and diaspora-run trading businesses.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Makkah Pact Allies Hold Emergency Riyadh Talks as Houthi Attacks Escalate
articles.excerpt: The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement's political and defence committee will meet in Riyadh next week to decide next steps on Houthi attacks against Saudi Arabia, while Iran has proposed a political track as an alternative to military action.
articles.image_caption: Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, where Makkah Pact allies held emergency talks as Houthi attacks escalated.
articles.nri_angle: Millions of Indian workers live in Saudi Arabia and the Gulf, including in Jeddah, Taif and Yanbu named in missile alerts, and Indian Hajj/Umrah pilgrims travel to Mecca — a city Saudi Arabia says the Houthis have targeted.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 17-Year-Old Held in Lucknow After Mother Killed in Family Dispute
articles.excerpt: Police say a 17-year-old boy in Lucknow fatally attacked his 42-year-old mother with an iron wrench during an argument, then called his father and the police himself. The teenager is in custody and being questioned.
articles.image_caption: A forensic investigator in protective gear examines a crime scene marked with police tape. Lucknow police said a forensic team examined the family residence after the teenager reported the killing.
articles.nri_angle: No direct diaspora angle.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Manchester City Verdict Strains Britain's Diplomatic Ties With the UAE
articles.excerpt: The UAE has warned London that sanctions against the Abu Dhabi-owned club could cool future investment, while British ministers privately question whether senior Emirati figures knew of the £900 million financial misconduct.
articles.image_caption: Manchester City's Etihad Stadium in Manchester, with its distinctive cable-stayed roof masts visible. The Abu Dhabi-owned club was found guilty of 130 breaches of Premier League financial rules, a verdict now straining diplomatic ties between the UK and the UAE.
articles.nri_angle: The UAE hosts one of the largest Indian communities in the world, and friction over London-Abu Dhabi investment flows matters to the diaspora in both countries.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Bangkok Struggles With Worst Flooding in 15 Years as Water Recedes
articles.excerpt: Some 320 mm of rain in two to three days left waist-deep water across the capital, killed at least eight nationwide, stranded Thai Airways passengers, and could shave 0.3 points off GDP growth.
articles.image_caption: Floodwaters recede in Bangkok after the city's worst flooding in 15 years.
articles.nri_angle: Bangkok is a major destination for Indian travellers; New Delhi flights were cancelled and baggage chaos at Suvarnabhumi hit Indian passengers hardest, while Bangkok's Indian trading community sits in the wholesale districts expected to take the heaviest economic hit.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: NASA Chief Warns China Could Shut U.S. Out of Lunar South Pole
articles.excerpt: Administrator Jared Isaacman said China's delayed Chang'e 7 mission targeted the same Shackleton Crater the U.S. wants, and safety exclusion zones could lock American missions out of the water-ice-rich terrain.
articles.image_caption: NASA's chief warns China could shut the U.S. out of the lunar south pole.
articles.nri_angle: India is an Artemis Accords signatory and Indian media reported NASA invited ISRO into the moon base program, placing India's space agency among the partners defining lunar norms.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Rubio Orders Iran's Delegation Out of New York as Talks Stall
articles.excerpt: U.S. officials say Iran's U.N. team had "overstayed their welcome" after indirect talks on the war and the Strait of Hormuz reached an impasse; Tehran insists the departure was pre-scheduled.
articles.image_caption: Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi speaks at the United Nations in New York. Secretary of State Marco Rubio ordered Iran's delegation to leave the city as nuclear talks stalled.
articles.nri_angle: The Hormuz standoff affects oil prices tied to India's imports, and the Qatari mediation runs through Doha, home to one of the region's largest Indian expatriate communities.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Iran Weighs Nuclear Options as U.S. Pressure Mounts and Talks Stall
articles.excerpt: Tehran's leadership openly debates pursuing a nuclear weapon or seeking sanctions relief as Washington's naval blockade and strikes tighten, and Israel warns an Iranian move could spiral out of control.
articles.image_caption: Iran weighs its nuclear options as U.S. pressure mounts and talks stall.
articles.nri_angle: A sustained conflict in the Strait of Hormuz threatens India's oil imports and fuel prices, while millions of Indian workers in Gulf states sit within range of Iranian missiles.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
